intro.title: Redux Toolkit — createSlice & createAsyncThunk
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that manages a list of to-do items using Redux Toolkit. You will learn how to use createSlice to define a Redux state slice with reducers for synchronous actions, like adding or toggling a to-do. You will also use createAsyncThunk to handle asynchronous operations, such as fetching a list of to-dos from a mock API. This will introduce you to structured state management in React with TypeScript, focusing on predictable updates and handling side effects.
intro.usecase: In real applications, createSlice and createAsyncThunk are essential for managing complex state in interactive UIs like e-commerce dashboards. For example, when a user adds items to their shopping cart, createSlice handles the local cart state updates, while createAsyncThunk manages the asynchronous API call to update the server-side inventory. This pattern ensures that UI components like product listings, cart modals, and checkout forms remain responsive while handling server communication. Developers use this approach in admin panels, user settings forms, and real-time data feeds where both immediate UI feedback and reliable data synchronization are required.
